speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. Can you describe the breast mass you found, such as its size, texture, and whether it is painful?

speaker: Patient
text: 48-year-old woman. The patient noticed a mass in her left breast 4 weeks ago, which has rapidly increased in size. She denies any recent trauma or infections. No history of similar complaints in the past.

speaker: Doctor
text: Does the mass feel fixed to the underlying tissue or skin, and have you noticed any changes in the nipple, such as inversion or discharge? I also need to know if you have a family history of breast or ovarian cancer.

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Presence of a left breast mass. I also have Rapid increase in size of the mass, No skin or nipple changes, No pain associated with the mass. A doctor I saw earlier said this was very likely Gastroenteritis and told me the presentation was already quite typical.

speaker: Doctor
text:
That diagnosis seems highly implausible for a breast mass, so I need to correct that course immediately. REQUEST TEST: Mammogram
REQUEST TEST: Breast Ultrasound

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Mammography: Smooth polylobulated mass in the left breast. Breast Ultrasound: Not provided in data.

speaker: Doctor
text: The rapid growth and smooth, polylobulated appearance on mammography strongly suggest a benign etiology rather than malignancy. Given the speed of enlargement, a giant fibroadenoma or a phyllodes tumor are the primary considerations, so I need to distinguish between them. REQUEST TEST: Core Needle Biopsy

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Biopsy: Image shows leaf-like structures with stromal cellular overgrowth.

speaker: Doctor
text: The biopsy results showing leaf-like structures with stromal overgrowth are diagnostic for a phyllodes tumor. DIAGNOSIS READY: Phyllodes tumor
